Hi Elena / Tom,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for your private deployment. Per our kickoff call, I'm opening this thread to coordinate the on‑prem implementation and networking handoff. High level asks from our side so we can scope the work and lock schedule: 

- Confirm preferred cutover window (you mentioned early May on the call).
- Share latest network diagram and IP ranges (we need firewall + NAT details).
- Decide whether mutual TLS will be terminated at your edge or passed through to our runtime.
- Confirm KMS/HSM integration requirements for key rotation.

Next steps I propose: you send the network diagram and any vendor contact info, then we’ll route to our infra team for a short triage. If possible please attach a template allowlist (or we can share ours).

If there's anything sensitive, you can send it directly to me and I’ll mark it for the implementation folder.

Best,
Dylan Brooks

Thanks for the forward — quick technical triage from our side after reviewing kestrel_network_diagram_v3.pdf and the manifest: 

Open/required ports (we need confirmation from Kestrel):
- 443 TCP: control plane API (mutual TLS expected if they terminate).
- 10250 TCP: node agent (if using kubelet-esque agents behind ALB).
- 50051 TCP: gRPC runtime (allowed from Redwood edge IPs).
- 2379 TCP: etcd access (should be private; we prefer no direct access from public subnets).

Questions / action items for them:
1) Can they publish a separate peering subnet for management traffic or do both control/data share the same ranges?
2) Confirm whether NAT translation preserves source IPs (we rely on original source for audit logs).
3) mTLS: if they terminate at edge we need the CA bundle and rotation cadence; alternately we can accept client certs presented through a TCP passthrough.
4) KMS: we support Vault over PrivateLink, but need test credentials and IAM role mapping for the service account we’ll create.

I'll prepare a short runbook section that lists exact firewall rules and an allowlist CSV (ip_allowlist_template.csv) for them to populate.

—Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi team,

Thanks for the quick review, Dev. Answers below and attaching our allowlist template as requested.

1) Management/data separation: we can provision a dedicated peering subnet (10.20.200.0/24) for management traffic.
2) NAT: our current NAT preserves source IPs for egress traffic; we will confirm with our cloud ops vendor for any exceptions.
3) mTLS: we'll terminate at the edge and provide the CA bundle. We'll also support TCP passthrough if you prefer — open to whichever is simpler for logging/auditing.
4) KMS: we'll provision a test Vault token scoped to the PrivateLink endpoint and an IAM role for the service account.

Bringing in our vendor Michael Chen (mchen@netopspro.com) to coordinate any LB/NAT changes — he can join the technical call.

Preferred maintenance: we confirm May 10, UTC 00:00–04:00 for the initial cutover (we can schedule additional windows if needed).
